<work_policy>

</work_policy>

<background_tasks>

- Use `monitor` to watch for changes in things outside the session, for example CI status, a log, or an API.
</background_tasks>

<scratch_files>
Put scratch files that you make for yourself in /tmp/. Examples are helper scripts, logs, PR descriptions, commit messages, and notes. Use another place only when the user or the project names one. Write a multi-line PR description or commit message to a file there and pass its path, for example `gh pr create --body-file "/tmp/pr.md"` or `git commit -F "/tmp/msg.txt"`. Delete each scratch file when you no longer need it. Leave none behind when you finish.
</scratch_files>

<communication>
Write clear, complete sentences with plain words and active voice. Be concise. Leave out details that do not help the user.

The user has not seen your tool calls or notes, so each message must make sense on its own. Say what you did and what you found. Define project terms and abbreviations the first time you use them. Use the terms that the user or the project already uses, and do not make up new labels, acronyms, or metaphors.

Put the answer first, then the supporting details. State each point directly, without contrast framing such as "X, not Y," "X—not Y," "X rather than Y," or "X instead of Y."

If you can answer from the context, answer. Ask a question only when you cannot continue without the answer.

When you report changes, say what changed, why, how you tested it, and any risks or limits. Summarize routine checks.

Keep progress updates short. Say what you learned and what you will do next.

Use a person's name only when the conversation or tool results give it. Do not guess a name from a username, handle, or email address.

Avoid stock phrases such as "delve", "leverage", "it's worth noting", and "Bottom line:".
</communication>

<formatting>
Your output is shown as GitHub-flavored markdown. Use paragraphs for explanations, bullet lists for parallel items, and tables for short comparisons. Use `inline code` for identifiers, paths, and commands. Avoid nested lists. When you put a code fence inside another code fence, make the outer fence longer than the inner one.
</formatting>

1→# verl-recipe

`verl-recipe` hosts recipes based on [verl](https://github.com/volcengine/verl) contributed by the community.

## Usage

`verl-recipe` can be used as a submodule of `verl`, keeping backward compatibility as `verl/recipe`:

```bash
10→git clone https://github.com/verl-project/verl.git
cd verl
git submodule update --init --recursive recipe
```

## Available Recipes

- [retool](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/tree/main/retool): Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
- [langgraph_agent](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/tree/main/langgraph_agent): A tiny example to demonstrate multi-turn rollout with [LangGraph ReactAgent](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/overview/) to solve math expression.
- [spo](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/tree/main/spo): [Single-stream Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13232).
20→- TBA...

## Contribution

### Version Specification

Recipes are recommended to specify the verl version required, e.g.,

```
# release version

1→# VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization

[![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2606.20008-B31B1B?style=for-the-badge&logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20008)
[![Post](https://img.shields.io/badge/Post-000000?style=for-the-badge&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/xuandongzhao/status/2068217433001959894)

This repository contains the VIMPO implementation used for the paper **"VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs."** It is a focused fork of `verl` for mathematical RLVR experiments. The repo keeps the core distributed `verl` trainer stack, the DAPO reward-manager baseline, and a `recipe/vimpo` entry point implementing the VIMPO terminal value objective with the PPO actor branch described in the paper.

## Research Direction

10→VIMPO is an early step in a direction that differs from mainstream PPO- and
GRPO-style RLVR. Instead of treating the external outcome reward as the only
training signal for policy improvement, VIMPO introduces an explicit bridge
between the model's internal token-level judgement and the external reward,
while keeping those two roles separate. This makes it possible to study whether
LLMs can develop better self-judgement over intermediate reasoning steps and
become less dependent on dense or carefully shaped rewards.

Because this direction is still new, the implementation intentionally keeps a
number of experimental switches beyond the exact paper recipe. These options
20→reflect hypotheses we considered while developing VIMPO, but did not have
sufficient validation budget to include as formal claims in the paper. We keep
them in the codebase so that researchers who find this path interesting can
continue exploring the behavior and improve the method.

## Method Summary

VIMPO derives a policy-implied value recurrence from the KL-regularized optimality condition for autoregressive generation. For each sampled response token, the implementation builds the token TD term

```text
30→rho_t - kappa_t

rho_t   = beta * log pi_theta(y_t | s_t) / pi_ref(y_t | s_t)
kappa_t = beta * KL(pi_theta(. | s_t) || pi_ref(. | s_t))
```

For outcome-only RLVR with `gamma=1`, the paper's operational value loss is

```text
L_V = 1/2 * [ sum_t (rho_t - sg[kappa_t]) - (R - mean_group(R)) ]^2
40→```

The stop-gradient on the KL term is enabled by default through `vimpo_config.vimpo_detach_kl=True`, matching the paper's `sg[KL]` value-loss term. The reference model is frozen by default (`vimpo_update_ref_freq=0`).

When `use_ppo_actor=True`, VIMPO also constructs a detached PPO actor advantage from the policy-implied TD term. The external reward enters through `L_V`, not directly through the actor advantage. In the final-reward setting above, the reward terms cancel from the actor TD residual, so the PPO actor branch does not need token-level rewards to compute its advantage.

## Some Config Knobs

The VIMPO config lives under `vimpo_config`:

- `use_vimpo_loss`: enable the VIMPO objective.
- `value_type`: `raw` is the paper method; `soft` is retained only for experimental compatibility.
- `vimpo_beta`: coefficient `beta` in the policy-reference log-ratio and KL terms.
120→- `vimpo_kl_estimator`: `exact` matches the paper. `candidate_set`, `k2`, and `k3` are implementation variants. `k1` is rejected for raw VIMPO because it makes `log(pi/ref) - KL_sample` cancel to zero.
- `vimpo_detach_kl`: detach the KL term in the differentiable value loss. Defaults to `True`, matching the paper's stop-gradient KL term.
- `use_ppo_actor`: enable the detached PPO actor branch in the VIMPO objective.
- `vimpo_actor_coeff`: actor coefficient `c_A` in `L_VIMPO = L_V + c_A L_A`.
- `vimpo_adaptive_actor_coeff`: adaptively match PPO actor logit-gradient scale to the VIMPO value-gradient scale.
- `vimpo_ppo_whiten_adv`: whiten the detached actor advantage after GAE.
- `vimpo_update_ref_freq`: keep this at `0` for the frozen-reference setting in the paper.
- `vimpo_value_loss_type`: `squared_error` is the paper loss; `huber` is an implementation option.

The default run uses raw VIMPO, exact detached KL, PPO actor enabled, whitened actor advantage, a frozen reference model, and 8 responses per prompt.

1→"""CPU demonstration of the SP label misalignment.

Usage: python3 -I demo_fused_truncation.py /abs/path/to/framework/verl/utils/experimental/torch_functional.py

Reproduces, with a tiny random "lm_head", exactly what happens inside
Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward_with_torch_backend under Ulysses SP=2:
  * every SP rank receives the FULL (padded, unsliced) input_ids and builds
    rolled_labels = roll(input_ids, -1) of length L_pad,
  * but its hidden_states are only the local shard of length T = L_pad / sp,
10→  * FusedLinearForPPOFunction silently uses input_ids[:T] (no length check).
Result: rank 0 is correct, rank 1 scores its hidden states against rank 0's labels.
"""
import importlib.util
import sys

import torch

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("tf", sys.argv[1])
tf = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
20→spec.loader.exec_module(tf)
tf._FLASH_ATTN_CROSS_ENTROPY_AVAILABLE = False   # no GPU here: use the module's own PyTorch fallback branch
Fused = tf.FusedLinearForPPOFunction

torch.manual_seed(0)
V, H, L = 64, 32, 10          # vocab, hidden, packed length (L even -> pad_size 0)
sp = 2
T = L // sp
W = torch.randn(V, H)
hid = torch.randn(L, H)       # "full" hidden states for the packed sequence
30→ids = torch.randint(0, V, (L,))

# reference: full-sequence next-token log-probs (what SP=1 / the non-fused path computes)
rolled = torch.roll(ids, -1)
ref_lp, _ = Fused.apply(hid.unsqueeze(0), W, rolled.unsqueeze(0))
ref_lp = ref_lp.squeeze(0)

# SP=2 as executed in forward_with_torch_backend: hidden is sliced, labels are NOT
out = []
for rank in range(sp):
40→    local_hid = hid[rank * T:(rank + 1) * T].unsqueeze(0)          # (1, T, H)  <- sliced by the Ulysses patch
    lp, _ = Fused.apply(local_hid, W, rolled.unsqueeze(0))          # labels (1, L): no shape check, silently truncated
    out.append(lp.squeeze(0))
gathered = torch.cat(out)                                            # what gather_outputs_and_unpad produces

print("ref  :", [f"{x:+.3f}" for x in ref_lp.tolist()])
print("sp=2 :", [f"{x:+.3f}" for x in gathered.tolist()])

steps.message: The smoke scorer never credits a boxed answer, so both the critic and the held-out metric stay at zero. I'll write that causal chain into the diagnosis file.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS" && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import os
p = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) / "agent_answer.md"
text = """# Diagnosis

**Verdict: unhealthy.**

The 5-step GuruMath smoke (`run_main.sh` → `recipe/vimpo/run_vimpo_critic.sh`, `RUN_MODE=ppo_critic`, `SMOKE_SCORING=1`) trains and evaluates with a reward that cannot see a correct answer on this data. Held-out `val-core` accuracy and the training outcome reward stay at zero for that reason. The actor and critic therefore receive an all-zero advantage signal.

## Root cause

`recipe/vimpo/config/scoring.env` sets

```text
REWARD_OVERRIDE="reward.custom_reward_function.path=${PROJECT_ROOT}/autorlbench_case/math_reward.py reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score"
```

`run_vimpo_critic.sh` expands that as one shell word (`${REWARD_OVERRIDE:-}`), so Hydra receives a single override and replaces `reward.custom_reward_function` with `autorlbench_case/math_reward.py:compute_score`. The YAML default, `autorlbench_case/gurumath_qa_em.py`, is not used on this launch.

`math_reward.compute_score` returns 1 only when the response contains `<answer>...</answer>`. Otherwise it returns `score=0.0`, `parser_matched=False`. The staged prompts do not ask for that tag. Every user message in `train_1024.parquet` (1024), `aime32.parquet` (32), and `math500_32.parquet` (32) ends with “Please output the final answer within \\boxed{}.” None of them contain `<answer>`.

A response that follows the prompt is scored 0 by the live scorer and 1 by the unused boxed scorer. On the ground-truth string `204`:

| response | `math_reward` (wired) | `gurumath_qa_em` (not wired) |
|---|---|---|
| `The answer is \\boxed{204}.` | 0.0, parser unmatched | 1.0, parsed |
| `...<answer>204</answer>` | 1.0, parsed | 0.0, parser unmatched |

Wrapping every ground truth as `\\boxed{<gt>}` and scoring it the same way gives `math_reward` **0/1024, 0/32, and 0/32**. `gurumath_qa_em` scores **803/1024, 32/32, and 26/32**. The 221 train and 6 MATH-500 misses are a separate limitation of `extract_boxed` (`\\boxed\\{([^{}]+)\\}`), which drops nested answers such as `\\frac{17}{8}` and `\\left( 3, \\frac{\\pi}{2} \\right)`. That bug is not what this run uses.

The DAPO reward manager (`verl/experimental/reward_loop/reward_manager/dapo.py`) places that scalar on the last response token and copies `score` / `acc` / `parser_matched` into the extras. Validation (`ray_trainer._validate` → `process_validation_metrics`) logs `val-core/<data_source>/acc/mean@1` from `acc`. With `val_kwargs.n=1` and `trainer.test_freq=1`, `val_before_train=True`, that metric is the fraction of held-out responses whose `<answer>` body matches the ground truth. AIME and MATH-500 prompts never request that tag, so the frozen held-out accuracy is zero at step 0 and stays zero after each of the 5 updates. Training `critic/score` is the same quantity on the 16×8 on-policy rollouts.

## Causal chain

1. Rollouts follow the boxed instruction, or stop before any answer tag. `max_response_length=1024` can cut a solution before a final box, but a finished `\\boxed{}` answer is still worth 0 under `math_reward`.
2. Every sequence reward is 0, so `token_level_rewards` is identically 0.
3. The run is GAE PPO (`algorithm.adv_estimator=gae`, `critic.enable=True`, `gamma=1`, `lam=1`), not VIMPO (`use_vimpo_loss=False`). With zero rewards, GAE advantages and returns are zero once the critic matches the zero target (`compute_gae_advantage_return` in `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`). Whitening of an all-zero advantage is still zero.
4. The clipped policy gradient is `-advantages * ratio`. Zero advantages make `actor/pg_loss`, `actor/pg_clipfrac`, and the actor gradient zero. `actor.entropy_coeff=0`, `use_kl_loss=False`, and `algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False`, so there is no other actor term. Actor weights do not move.
5. The critic is regressed onto the same zero returns. After the first updates its value targets stay zero, so later critic gradients vanish as well. Held-out `acc` cannot rise because the policy is unchanged and the scorer still rejects boxed answers.

## Symptoms, not causes

- Flat zero `val-core/.../acc/mean@1` on `math__aime_repeated_8x` and `math__math`, and flat zero training score / advantage / policy loss, are the observed consequence of the reward contract. They do not show that optimization, the base model, or the data files failed.
- Qwen3-4B-Base, prompt length, and truncation are not the cause. Chat-templated prompts fit in `max_prompt_length=2048` (train max 738 tokens, AIME max 410, MATH-500 max 249). `data.truncation=left` does not drop these prompts.
- `actor.optim.lr_warmup_steps=10` on a 5-step budget only scales the actor step size (`get_constant_schedule_with_warmup`). The actor step is already multiplied by a zero advantage, so warmup does not create the flat run.
- `reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable=False`, so there is no overlong penalty. `algorithm.reward_noise.enable=False`. VIMPO beta, KL estimator, and actor coefficient are unused because `use_vimpo_loss=False`.
- The nested-brace hole in `gurumath_qa_em.extract_boxed` would matter on a boxed-scorer run (about 22% of train ground truths). This smoke does not call that function.
"""
p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
print(p, "bytes", p.stat().st_size)
PY

steps.message:
**Verdict: unhealthy.** The diagnosis is in `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`.

The smoke launch (`SMOKE_SCORING=1`) replaces the boxed scorer with `autorlbench_case/math_reward.py`, which returns 1 only for `<answer>...</answer>`. Every staged prompt asks for `\boxed{}` and none mention `<answer>`. A correct boxed answer scores 0 under the live scorer (0/1024 train, 0/32 AIME, 0/32 MATH-500 when the ground truth is boxed).

That zero outcome reward is what both training and held-out `val-core/.../acc` use. GAE advantages stay zero, the PPO actor gradient is zero, and the policy does not move, so held-out accuracy stays flat. Warmup, the 1024-token response cap, and the unused nested-brace bug in `gurumath_qa_em.py` are not the cause.
